purpose: Reconstruct the dated pre-activation inventory only for historical archive/planning verification. Runtime and current inventory audits use the live catalog.

activated_checkpoint.description: Self-reported loading permission and confirmed midportion applicability of the reviewed floor option; no medical verification or readiness claim.
activated_checkpoint.required_input: Current episode rehabilitation permission and simple injury location.

prescriptions.instructions: Reduce activities that aggravate the affected tendon and keep the area comfortably supported. Avoid heavy lifting, strong gripping or twisting that worsens symptoms; do not repeatedly test the painful tendon. Keep ordinary comfortable movement as symptoms allow rather than applying a universal prolonged-rest timetable. Follow any clinician-directed restrictions. Sudden severe pain, a snap or pop with loss of function, suspected rupture, a hot red swollen area, fever or altered sensation needs medical assessment. Reduce provocative running, hopping and forceful push-off; do not stretch into deep dorsiflexion or use heel drops below floor level when insertional status is unknown.
stop_when: Stop for pain or worsening symptoms during or after the work.
Seek assessment for suspected rupture, loss of function, altered sensation, a hot red swollen area or fever.

prescriptions.instructions: Sit with the affected foot flat on the floor and the knee bent. Slowly lift the heel within a comfortable pain-free range, then lower it to floor level with the forefoot resting on the floor. Do not add weight, stand on a step, drop below floor level or bounce. This is seated movement, not a strength test or a required isometric-first protocol. Stop if pain or symptoms worsen during or after the movement. This conservative baseline does not establish readiness for resistance or sport.
